podcast.body: During the recording of "She Sells Sanctuary," drummer Nigel Preston, who had a severe drinking problem, showed up intoxicated and struggled to play. Singer Ian Astbury and guitarist Billy Duffy gradually removed pieces of his drum set, leaving him with just a snare, bass drum, and hi-hats. This limitation forced a much more rhythmic, straight-ahead 4/4 beat with minimal snare fills, inadvertently creating the song's distinctive, effective drumming. "The result was a song that was much more rhythmic, much more straight ahead than anything to call it ever done."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This enduring alt-rock song from the 80s was the big single from The Cult's "Love" album. It was recorded in March 1985, and despite its success, the song was initially buried deep on the record, appearing as Track 9 on the CD (Side 2 on the album). "You didn't get to She Sells Sanctuary until Track 9 on the CD."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
